A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Learn2Synth paper, with all 16 pages and supplementary Sections 6–15 available. Text, equations, tables, embedded images, and rendered pages support reliable comparison; differences are confined to the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its link.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic-noise and intensity-nonuniformity experiments, real-MRI segmentation evaluations, and supplementary experiments in Sections 9–12.

after.justification: v4 reports the same original empirical results, including segmentation scores in Tables 1–9 and the unpaired-segmentation experiment in Section 10.

M1.justification: The alternating synthetic/real training passes, hypergradient updates, parametric and nonparametric augmentation models, and supplementary unpaired adaptation are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions retain identical synthetic noise/INU scenarios and evaluations using OASIS/OASIS3, ABIDE, Buckner39, and FLASH scans, including the unpaired setting.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding experiment, including Naive/Optimized SynthSeg, Supervised UNet, SAMSEG, Mixed/Finetuned SynthSeg, and AdvChain.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, Dice evaluation, 2D training, sample sizes, validation-based model selection, and the fixed-test-size comparison in Section 12 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The noise/INU sensitivity tests, cross-contrast evaluations, validation-dependence analysis in Section 9, and backbone comparison in Section 11 are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is identical, including the plus/minus entries in Tables 6, 7, and 9 and Section 10. No seed, repeated-run, or statistical-procedure information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–9 and qualitative results are identical. For example, both versions report an unpaired-segmentation Dice score of 0.874 ± 0.0104 in Section 10.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), the hypergradient derivation, and the mathematical assumptions defining noise and intensity-nonuniformity augmentation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about learning augmentations through hypergradients, segmentation accuracy, and generalization to unseen contrasts.

C2.justification: Interpretations of learned parameters, validation sensitivity, and computational tradeoffs are unchanged. Sections 14–15 retain the same discussion of 2D evaluation, labeled-real-data requirements, and segmentation-only scope.

D1.justification: Sections 7, 8, and 13 retain identical preprocessing instructions, architecture details, optimizer settings, hardware, and training times. Code and software access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work Sections 2 and 6, all 90 references, and the positioning relative to augmentation, domain adaptation, and domain randomization are identical.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v3, dated 1 Aug 2025, to v4, dated 21 Apr 2026, with its link updated accordingly. All paper prose, headings, terminology, and section ordering remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5, Tables 1–9, captions, placement, and body layout are identical. Rendered-page differences are confined to the updated marginal version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and supplementary material are unchanged. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and associated link produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
